g12-economics-ue7-t1.overview: National Development Objectives and Strategies sits inside Macroeconomic Reforms in Ethiopia. Macroeconomic reforms in Ethiopia are the focus of Unit 7 of Grade 12 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it reviews national development plans from the Imperial period to the 2021 to 2030 reform agenda. Then it explains the home-grown economic reforms, both macroeconomic and structural. Finally, it examines fiscal decentralization. Students will also learn how macroeconomic reforms shape real-life development in Ethiopia.
objectives: Explain the national development objectives and strategies of Ethiopia.
Distinguish macroeconomic, sectoral, and structural reforms.
Explain fiscal decentralization and its trade-offs.
Assess the role of the private sector in the reform process.
g12-economics-ue7-t1.simple:
National Development Objectives and Strategies in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, development plans under the Imperial period from 1950 to 1974.
  • Then plans under the socialist period from 1974 to 1991.
  • Also plans under the FDRE.
  • Finally, the reform agenda for 2021 to 2030.
g12-economics-ue7-t1.detailed:
National Development Objectives and Strategies — the essentials. First, development plans under the Imperial period from 1950 to 1974. Then plans under the socialist period from 1974 to 1991. Also plans under the FDRE. Finally, the reform agenda for 2021 to 2030.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the national development objectives and strategies of Ethiopia.
  • Describe the home-grown economic reforms.
  • Distinguish macroeconomic, sectoral, and structural reforms.
  • Explain fiscal decentralization and its trade-offs.
  • Assess the role of the private sector in the reform process.
